_patient.note:
[1] The patient was admitted from transfer from hospital.
[2] The patient presented with postprocedural fever, hematuria, unspecified, and other fecal abnormalities.
[3] The primary diagnosis was gastric varices.
[4] The active diagnoses were gastric varices, portal vein thrombosis, acute respiratory failure with hypoxia, secondary esophageal varices without bleeding, portal hypertension, ileus, unspecified, coagulation defect, unspecified, gastrointestinal hemorrhage, unspecified, unspecified cirrhosis of liver, chronic viral hepatitis C, major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified, anxiety disorder, unspecified, essential (primary) hypertension, unspecified glaucoma, other diseases of stomach and duodenum, hepatopulmonary syndrome, postprocedural hypotension, nonrheumatic mitral (valve) insufficiency, and anemia, unspecified.
[5] The past medical history included dependence on supplemental oxygen.
[6] The procedures performed were bypass portal vein to lower vein with intraluminal device, percutaneous approach; extirpation of matter from portal vein, percutaneous approach; restriction of gastric vein with intraluminal device, percutaneous approach; insertion of endotracheal airway into trachea, via natural or artificial opening; and respiratory ventilation, 24-96 consecutive hours.
[7] The medications administered included influenza vaccine quadrivalent 0.5mL IM, chlorhexidine gluconate 0.12% oral rinse 15mL oral, heparin flush (10 units/ml) 1mL IV, sodium chloride 0.9% flush 10mL IV, furosemide 40mg IV, 0.9% sodium chloride 250mL IV drip, norepinephrine 8mg IV drip, propofol 200mg IV drip, sodium chloride 0.9% 1000mL IV, spironolactone 50mg PO/NG, 5% dextrose 250mL IV, potassium phosphate 15mmol IV, lorazepam 1mg PO/NG, folic acid 1mg PO/NG, thiamine 100mg PO/NG, 0.9% sodium chloride (mini bag plus) 100mL IV, cefTRIAXone 1gm IV, octreotide acetate 500mcg IV drip, iso-osmotic dextrose 200mL IV, vancomycin 1000mg IV, potassium chloride 40mEq IV, calcium carbonate 500mg PO/NG, bag 1bag IV, magnesium sulfate 2gm IV, NS 100mL IV, metronidazole 500mg IV, pantoprazole 40mg PO, neutra-phos 1pkt PO/NG, sterile water 150mL IV, ramelteon 8mg PO/NG, calcium gluconate 2g IV, cepacol (sore throat lozenge) 2loz PO, sertraline 100mg PO/NG, sarna lotion 1appl TP, fentanyl citrate 25-100mcg IV, albumin 25% (12.5g/50mL) 75g IV, vial 1vial IV, vitamin D 2000unit PO/NG, trazodone 25mg PO/NG, acetaminophen 1000mg PO/NG, soln 50mL IV drip, heparin 5000unit SC, and potassium chloride 40mEq IV.
[8] The microbiology results showed yeast in the urine and sputum.
[9] The services provided were medical intensive care unit (MICU), transplant, and surgical intensive care unit (SICU).
[10] The patient was discharged alive to home health care.
